candidates.text:
Blood in the streets.

The problem is a simple fallacy: ig I'm not urging everyone to do what they think, I must think the opposite.

No so.

(If I did, I'd short gold and silver.)

It's the lack of conviction that keeps me on the sidelines.

Not so for other commodities...

candidates.author: Lobo Tiggre
candidates.text:
No.

That's exactly my point: Things could take off without me and I'm okay with that.

The possibility does not make me want to buy high and hope to sell higher.

And if gold and silver go nuts, something else will tank—that's what I'll look to buy.

candidates.author: Lobo Tiggre
candidates.text:
No thank you.

People don’t seem to understand or believe that I have no problem with this train leaving without me.

I’m looking for “blood in the streets,” not, “cheaper than a few months ago.”

If that’s in something other than gold and silver stocks, so be it.

candidates.author: Otavio Costa
candidates.text:
Here is the wild part about the Treasury market today:

The US debt‑to‑GDP ratio is now roughly on par with World War II — actually a bit worse.

However, back then:

Nearly half of all Treasuries were backed by gold.

Today, it’s about 3%.

That’s how deep the problem runs.
